title: Bench: tx_ready_i is pinned high, so the TX backpressure path is unobserved
body:
[R1]

Found by a deliberate sweep for bench inputs pinned to a constant, run while building the #28 fix. That sweep exists because `txts_seq_i` turned out to be pinned to 0 for every frame, which is why the engine could ignore the egress-stamp tag unnoticed: while a bench input is constant, an implementation that reads it and one that ignores it are indistinguishable to the suite, and green says nothing about the property. `tx_ready_i` is the same shape.

## What is wrong

The engine bench drives `tx_ready_i` to a constant 1 and never deasserts it, so the TX backpressure path is never exercised. The parent drives it dynamically: `eng_tx_ready_w = gbo_ready_w | ~gbo_valid_w` at `KL_gptp_shadow.sv:499` in kebag-logic/milan-fpga, so on real hardware the engine does meet a deasserting ready, and it meets it more often under load, since the control lane is shared.

The consequence is not that a defect is known to exist. It is that no test in this repository could see one. Anything the engine does wrong when ready deasserts mid-frame (stalling incorrectly, dropping or truncating a frame, corrupting the serializer state, losing or double-counting an egress claim now that #28 makes claims stateful) passes the suite today.

## Why it matters more after #28

The #28 fix makes the transmit path carry per-transmitter claim state across the interval between hand-over and the returning timestamp. Backpressure lengthens exactly that interval, and it is the interval whose width the parent cannot yet bound (kebag-logic/milan-fpga#213). A claim mechanism that is correct only while ready is always high is not obviously correct on the shipping fabric.

## Sweep result for the record

| input | bench drive | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `txts_seq_i` | constant 0 | the #28 defect; fixed there, the bench now reports the stamped frame's own sequenceId |
| `tx_ready_i` | constant 1, never deasserted | this issue |
| `rx_err_i` | constant 0 | constant in the parent too, deliberately (`KL_gptp_shadow.sv:447`, the frame FIFO never delivers a bad frame), and the parser suite exercises the arm directly; not a blind spot |
| `phc_ns_i`, the `rx_*` group, `rst_n` | driven live | dynamic |

## Acceptance

- [ ] The bench deasserts `tx_ready_i`, including mid-frame, for one beat and for many, and at the start of a frame so the first beat stalls.
- [ ] Under that backpressure every transmitted frame is still byte-correct and complete, the egress claim still matches its own transmitter, and no frame is lost, duplicated or truncated.
- [ ] A planted mutation that mishandles a deasserting ready goes red; if no such mutation can be written because the design is structurally immune, say so in the README with the reason, since that is a stronger result than a passing test.
- [ ] The pattern is applied deliberately rather than once: state in the bench README which engine inputs are constant by design and which are driven live, so the next constant-pinned input is a documented choice rather than an accident.

Related: #28, #31, kebag-logic/milan-fpga#213.
